pressReleaseTitle: India Ratings Affirms B.G. Shirke Construction Technology at ‘IND A’/Stable; Limits Enhanced
issuerName: B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd.
overview: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) has affirmed B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt Ltd’s (BGSCTPL)’s Long-Term Issuer Rating at ‘IND A’. The Outlook is Stable. The instrument-wise rating actions are as follows:
keyRatingDrivers:
Sound Financial Profile: BGSCTPL’s financial profile remained sound post the amalgamation of Five Stars Bulkcarriers Pvt Ltd (FSBCPL). Its revenue recovered to INR31.04 billion post a fall to INR25.21 billion in FY17. The fall was due to the delayed commencement of large housing projects awarded by Delhi Development Authority owing to deferred approvals, which were finally received in June 2017. Revenue from construction contracts accounted for about 93% of the revenue in FY18.

 

Moreover, its EBITDA margin significantly increased to 19.4% in FY18 from 15.4% in FY17 as one-time escalation claims were received from erstwhile projects. Excluding the one-time claims, the margin improved to 16.5% from the FY17 level. Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL to register healthy revenue growth for FY19-FY20 in view of strong medium-term revenue visibility.

 

Robust-but-Concentrated Order Book: At end-August 2018, BGSCTPL had an unexecuted order book of INR140.6 billion (end-June 2017: INR149 billion), which translates into 4.5x of FY18 revenue (FY17: 5.89x). Customer concentration remained high, considering Delhi Development Authority and Maharashtra Housing and Development Authority represented 45% (end-June 2017: 49.8%) and 47% (65.2%) of the order book as of August 2018, respectively.

 

Moreover, the top 10 project concentration in the order book as of August 2018 was high at 60.6% but was stable compared with the 60.8% in FY17. Slow-moving projects, which are typically classified as projects awarded over FY09-FY14, accounted for 11% of the order book at end-August 2018 (end-June 2017: 3%). As at end-August 2018, about 42% of the unexecuted projects were received in FY16 and the majority of these orders were from Delhi Development Authority, for which the company received delayed execution orders.

 

As confirmed by the management, the majority of its order book has execution orders. Thus, no delay in project execution is likely in the near to medium term. BGSCTPL continues to have a strong competitive position in the prefabricated housing industry, with an established operating record of over 30 years. The strong competitive position benefits the company in terms of meeting prequalification criteria when bidding for new projects of similar types.

 

Continued Strong Credit Metrics: BGSCTPL’s net adjusted leverage (adjusted net debt/operating EBITDAR) improved to 1.46x in FY18 from 1.80x in FY17, primarily driven by a rise in EBITDA. The improvement in the leverage was despite an increase in gross debt to INR10 billion in FY8 from INR7.8 billion in FY17, as the company availed additional term loans to purchase additional plant and equipment to set up factories in Delhi, Pune and Mumbai. Its gross interest coverage (operating EBITDA/gross interest expense) improved to 3.32x in FY18 from 2.31x in FY17 on account a proportionately higher rise in EBITDA than that in interest expenses.

 

Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL’s credit metrics to sustain at the same levels in the near to medium term on account of healthy medium-term revenue visibility.

 

Adequate Liquidity: BGSCTPL’s cash flow from operations improved to INR1.6 billion in FY18 from negative INR0.3 billion on account of the rise in EBITDA. However, capex incurred to set up factories in Delhi, Pune and Mumbai led to a continued negative free cash flow of INR1.3 billion in FY18 (FY17: negative INR0.9).  However, liquidity was cushioned by the receipt of mobilisation advances of INR8.2 billion in FY18 (FY17: INR8.5 billion). Cash balances remained high at INR1.3 billion at FYE18 (FYE17: INR0.9 billion).

 

Moreover, BGSCTPL’s maximum use of its fund-based working capital limits was 43% and of its non-fund-based limits was 73% over the 12 months ended July 2018. As of November 2018, BGSCTPL had undrawn cash credit lines of INR5.3 billion and non-fund based limits of INR11.5 billion for use in FY19.

 

Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL’s debt service coverage ratio to remain comfortable at over 1.0x in FY19-FY20 for servicing interest and debt repayments.

 

Exposure to Group Entities: Given the weak financial profile of FSBCPL (which operates a fleet of four dry-bulk ships on a charter basis), it continued to receive support from BGSCTPL in the form of a corporate guarantee. BGSCTPL had applied for the amalgamation of FSBCPL; the amalgamation was completed in August 2017. Ind-Ra had consolidated the financial profiles of BGSCTPL and FSBCPL in the FY17 review to ascertain the impact of the amalgamation. No significant deterioration in the financial profile was witnessed post the amalgamation.

 

BGSCTPL extended support to group entities in the form of loans and advances of INR2.2 billion in FY18 (FY17: INR.2 billion). The majority of support was to Shirke Recreation Enterprise (‘IND BB’/Stable) as its operations are yet to pick up.
ratingSensitivities:
Positive: A substantial diversification in the customer base and project segments, while sustaining the credit metrics at the current levels, would be positive for the ratings.

Negative: BGSCTPL’s net adjusted leverage exceeding 2.25x, on a sustained basis, could lead to a negative rating action.
companyProfile:
Incorporated in 1955, BGSCTPL is the flagship company of the Pune-based Shirke Group. BGSCTPL is primarily engaged in the construction of housing projects for government agencies such as Delhi Development Authority, Maharashtra Housing and Development Authority, and City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Ltd.

descriptionAboutIndiaRating:
India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) is India's SEBI registered credit rating agency committed to providing India's credit markets accurate, timely, and prospective credit opinions. Built on a foundation of independent thinking, rigorous analytics, and an open and balanced approach towards credit research, Ind-Ra has grown rapidly during the past decade, gaining significant market presence in India's fixed income market.

Ind-Ra currently maintains coverage of corporate issuers, financial institutions (including banks and insurance companies), finance companies, urban local bodies, and structured finance and project finance companies.

Headquartered in Mumbai, Ind-Ra has seven branch offices located in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Pune. Ind-Ra is recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India.

Ind-Ra is a 100% owned subsidiary of the Fitch Group.
